# kuzco-alt-text

Generate alt text for an image using a local vision language model, exposed as an
[ellmer](https://ellmer.tidyverse.org/) tool by the kuzco R package.

## When to use

The user wants a textual description of an image: accessibility alt text, a caption,
or a quick summary of image contents for indexing or search.

## Setup

Register the tool on an ellmer chat. The model and provider are fixed at registration;
the LLM controls the image path, extra prompt text, and output language per call.

```r
library(kuzco)
library(ellmer)

chat <- chat_ollama(model = "qwen2.5vl")
chat$register_tool(tool_llm_image_alt_text())
```

To use a different model or a hosted provider, pass them to the constructor:

```r
chat$register_tool(tool_llm_image_alt_text(
  llm_model = "qwen2.5vl",
  provider = "ollama"
))
```

## Tool arguments (LLM-controlled)

- `image` (required): local file path to a jpeg, jpg, or png image.
- `additional_prompt` (optional): extra instructions appended to the image prompt,
  e.g. "focus on the people in the foreground".
- `language` (optional): output language, e.g. "English", "Spanish".

## Result

Compact JSON text describing the image, returned to the model as the tool result.
Relay the description to the user; do not invent details beyond what the tool returned.

## Example

> User: "Write alt text for img/photo.jpg"
> 1. Call `kuzco_image_alt_text` with `image = "img/photo.jpg"`.
> 2. Return the description as the alt text.

# kuzco-classification

Classify an image and describe its contents using a local vision language model,
exposed as an [ellmer](https://ellmer.tidyverse.org/) tool by the kuzco R package.

## When to use

The user wants to know what an image shows: its category, the primary and secondary
objects, a description, dominant colors, or class probabilities. This is the default
skill for "what is in this image?" questions.

## Setup

```r
library(kuzco)
library(ellmer)

chat <- chat_ollama(model = "qwen2.5vl")
chat$register_tool(tool_llm_image_classification())
```

## Tool arguments (LLM-controlled)

- `image` (required): local file path to a jpeg, jpg, or png image.
- `additional_prompt` (optional): extra instructions, e.g. "pay special attention to text on signs".
- `language` (optional): output language, e.g. "English".

## Result

Compact JSON text with `image_classification`, `primary_object`, `secondary_object`,
`image_description`, `image_colors`, and `image_proba_names` / `image_proba_values`.
Summarize the key fields for the user; quote the description verbatim when asked for detail.

## Example

> User: "What animal is in img/puppy.jpg?"
> 1. Call `kuzco_image_classification` with `image = "img/puppy.jpg"`.
> 2. Answer from `primary_object` and `image_description`, mentioning the classification and confidence.

# kuzco-custom

Run an arbitrary computer-vision prompt against an image using a local vision
language model, exposed as an [ellmer](https://ellmer.tidyverse.org/) tool by the
kuzco R package. This is the escape hatch for image tasks the specialized skills
do not cover.

## When to use

The task needs something from an image that classification, OCR, object recognition,
sentiment analysis, or alt text do not capture — e.g. "count the windows", "is anyone
wearing a red hat?", "describe the chart axes". Prefer a specialized skill when one fits;
use this one otherwise.

## Setup

```r
library(kuzco)
library(ellmer)

chat <- chat_ollama(model = "qwen2.5vl")
chat$register_tool(tool_llm_image_custom())
```

## Tool arguments (LLM-controlled)

- `image` (required): local file path to a jpeg, jpg, or png image.
- `image_prompt` (required): the prompt describing what to extract or describe about
  the image. Be specific: state exactly what to look for and what shape the answer
  should take.
- `system_prompt` (optional): persona/style steering, defaults to a terse computer
  vision assistant.

## Result

Compact JSON text with the model's structured response to the custom prompt.
Present it directly; do not reformat structured fields the user asked for.

## Example

> User: "How many bicycles are in img/street.jpg?"
> 1. Call `kuzco_image_custom` with `image = "img/street.jpg"` and
>    `image_prompt = "Count the bicycles visible in the image. Return the count and briefly describe where each one is."`.
> 2. Report the count and locations.

# kuzco-extract-text

Extract text visible in an image (OCR) using a local vision language model, exposed
as an [ellmer](https://ellmer.tidyverse.org/) tool by the kuzco R package.

## When to use

The user wants the text content of an image: screenshots, scanned documents, photos
of signs or labels, memes, charts with annotations. If the task is about the image
as a whole rather than its text, use kuzco-classification instead.

## Setup

```r
library(kuzco)
library(ellmer)

chat <- chat_ollama(model = "qwen2.5vl")
chat$register_tool(tool_llm_image_extract_text())
```

## Tool arguments (LLM-controlled)

- `image` (required): local file path to a jpeg, jpg, or png image.
- `additional_prompt` (optional): extra instructions, e.g. "only transcribe the headline".
- `language` (optional): output language, e.g. "English".

## Result

Compact JSON text with the extracted text and a confidence score. Reproduce the
transcribed text faithfully; flag low confidence to the user rather than silently
"fixing" unclear passages.

## Example

> User: "What does the sign say in img/sign.jpg?"
> 1. Call `kuzco_image_extract_text` with `image = "img/sign.jpg"`.
> 2. Quote the extracted text and note the confidence.

skills.desc: Recognize and locate instances of an object in an image with a local vision LLM. Wraps kuzco's tool_llm_image_recognition() ellmer tool. Use when the task needs finding, counting, or locating specific objects (faces, cars, animals) in an image.

# kuzco-recognition

Recognize and locate instances of an object in an image using a local vision
language model, exposed as an [ellmer](https://ellmer.tidyverse.org/) tool by the
kuzco R package.

## When to use

The user wants to find a specific kind of object in an image: faces, cars, dogs,
text regions. Counting instances and describing/locating each one. For general
"what is in this image?" questions, use kuzco-classification instead.

## Setup

```r
library(kuzco)
library(ellmer)

chat <- chat_ollama(model = "qwen2.5vl")
chat$register_tool(tool_llm_image_recognition())
```

## Tool arguments (LLM-controlled)

- `image` (required): local file path to a jpeg, jpg, or png image.
- `recognize_object` (optional): the object to recognize, e.g. "face", "car", "dog".
  Defaults to "face".
- `additional_prompt` (optional): extra instructions, e.g. "only count adults".
- `language` (optional): output language, e.g. "English".

## Result

Compact JSON text with `object_recognized`, `object_count`, `object_description`,
and `object_location`. Report the count first, then describe/locate instances.
If the count is zero, say so plainly rather than hedging.

## Example

> User: "How many faces are in img/group.jpg and where?"
> 1. Call `kuzco_image_recognition` with `image = "img/group.jpg"`, `recognize_object = "face"`.
> 2. Report the count and describe each location.

# kuzco-sentiment

Analyze the sentiment or mood conveyed by an image using a local vision language
model, exposed as an [ellmer](https://ellmer.tidyverse.org/) tool by the kuzco R
package.

## When to use

The user wants the emotional tone of an image: cheerful, somber, threatening,
calm. Useful for content moderation triage, marketing asset selection, or photo
curation. For factual descriptions of image contents, use kuzco-classification.

## Setup

```r
library(kuzco)
library(ellmer)

chat <- chat_ollama(model = "qwen2.5vl")
chat$register_tool(tool_llm_image_sentiment())
```

## Tool arguments (LLM-controlled)

- `image` (required): local file path to a jpeg, jpg, or png image.
- `additional_prompt` (optional): extra instructions, e.g. "consider cultural context".
- `language` (optional): output language, e.g. "English".

## Result

Compact JSON text with `image_sentiment`, `image_score`, `sentiment_description`,
and `image_keywords`. Lead with the sentiment label and score, then the description.
Present sentiment as the model's reading, not as ground truth.

## Example

> User: "What mood does img/sunset.jpg convey?"
> 1. Call `kuzco_image_sentiment` with `image = "img/sunset.jpg"`.
> 2. Report the sentiment, score, and description.
